t:
For the purposes of this title:
    (1) Groundwater remediation.—The term “groundwater remediation” means actions that are necessary to prevent, minimize, or mitigate damage to groundwater. 
    (2) Local water authority.—The term “local water authority” means the Santa Clara Valley Water District or a public water district, public water utility, public water planning agency, municipality, or Indian tribe located within the Santa Clara Valley; and a public water district, public water utility, public water planning agency, municipality, or Indian tribe located within the natural watershed of the Santa Ana river in the State of California. 
    (3) Remediation fund.—The term “Remediation Fund” means the California Basins Groundwater Remediation Fund established pursuant to section 803(a). 
    (4) Secretary.—The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

fable.w: This section only defines terms (groundwater remediation, local water authority, Remediation Fund, Secretary). The tempting reading is that naming municipalities, water districts, and Indian tribes signals outside-party involvement, but they are merely defined here. Nothing in the section requires or authorizes consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: The term “local water authority” means the Santa Clara Valley Water District or a public water district, public water utility, public water planning agency, municipality, or Indian tribe located within the Santa Clara Valley

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of definitions for terms used elsewhere in the statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties. While it defines 'local water authority' to include entities outside the federal government, the definition itself does not mandate their participation in a decision-making process.

Naming tribes and local water districts in a definition can look like participation, but no actual role in decision-making is set up here.

opus.b: 1. **Analysis.** The tempting reading is that this section involves outside parties because it defines "local water authority" to include water districts, municipalities and Indian tribes, all of which are outside the federal government. That reading fails because this is only a definitions section. It names who counts as a local water authority but sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Nothing here brings those entities into a federal decision.
